findings.label: Letter type
findings.text: Time-limited FoodShare warning: agency records show 1 of 3 time-limited months already used.

findings.label: Work requirement — three ways to meet it
findings.text: 1) Work ≥ 80 hours/month; 2) Participate in an allowable work program (FSET, W-2, WIOA) ≥ 80 hours/month; 3) Combined work + program totaling ≥ 80 hours/month.

findings.label: FSET option
findings.text: Enrolling in FSET is one way to meet the requirement. The letter says you must enroll and participate by the start of your third time-limited month. FSET provider: (414) 555-0142 or dhs.wisconsin.gov/foodshare/fset.htm.

findings.label: Exemptions listed in letter
findings.text: The letter lists possible exemptions: living with a child under 18 in the same household; primary caretaker for a dependent adult or child under 6 not in the home; physically or mentally unable to work (including long-term homelessness); pregnant; receiving/applied for unemployment insurance; in AODA treatment; enrolled at least half-time in higher education or high school (age 18+); enrolled in W-2 and complying; working 30+ hours/week or earning equivalent wages.

findings.label: How to report an exemption
findings.text: If you believe you meet an exemption, call the agency at 1-888-947-6583 to report it and ask what proof is needed. The agency decides whether the exemption applies.

findings.label: Deadline language
findings.text: The letter states you must enroll and participate in FSET 'by the start of your third time-limited FoodShare benefit month.' No calendar date is printed.

next_step.text: Call Milwaukee Enrollment Services at 1-888-947-6583 today to report any exemption you may qualify for, or to ask about FSET enrollment. The agency decides whether an exemption is approved or whether benefits continue.

tasks.text: Call Milwaukee Enrollment Services at 1-888-947-6583 to report any exemption you may qualify for and ask what proof is needed. The agency determines whether an exemption applies.
If you want to meet the work requirement through FSET, call the FSET provider at (414) 555-0142 or visit dhs.wisconsin.gov/foodshare/fset.htm to enroll and begin participating.
If reporting an exemption, gather supporting documents (e.g., proof of pregnancy, unemployment insurance application, school enrollment, medical documentation) before calling the agency.
If you disagree with the agency's determination, you have the right to request a fair hearing. Ask the agency about the hearing request process and deadline when you call.

passages.text: PIN: 0000000001 Date: 09/08/2026 Page 1 of 3 State of Wisconsin PIN #: 0000000001 Milwaukee Enrollment Services Phone Number: 1-888-947-6583 Fax Number: (414) 555-0100 The State of Wisconsin is an equal opportunity service provider. This letter contains information that affects your beneﬁts. If you need this material in a different format because of a disability or if you need this letter translated or explained in your own language, please call 1-888-947-6583. These services are free.

Important Information about Your Time-Limited FoodShare Beneﬁts Our records show that you are not meeting the work requirement for getting ongoing FoodShare beneﬁts and that you have already used one of your three time-limited FoodShare beneﬁt months. If you do not start meeting the work requirement or meet an exemption from the work requirement, you will use up your three time-limited FoodShare beneﬁt months, and your FoodShare beneﬁts will end.

One way that you can meet the work requirement is by taking part in the FoodShare Employment and Training (FSET) program. The FSET program is a free program that can help you build job skills and ﬁnd employment. If you want to meet the work requirement by taking part in the FSET program, you must enroll and take part in activities by the start of your third time-limited FoodShare beneﬁt month. Otherwise you will use up your three time-limited beneﬁt months, and your FoodShare beneﬁts will end.
To enroll in the FSET program or to get answers to your questions about FSET, call your FSET service provider at (414) 555-0142, or go to dhs.wisconsin.gov/foodshare/fset.htm.

If you are age 18 through 49 years old, with no minor children living in your home who are in the same FoodShare household, you may only get up to three months of FoodShare beneﬁts in a 36-month period, unless you meet the work requirement or meet an exemption from the work requirement.

PIN: 0000000001 Date: 09/08/2026 Page 2 of 3 How to Meet the Work Requirement There are three ways to meet the work requirement:
1. Work at least 80 hours each month.
2. Take part in an allowable work program, such as the FSET program, Wisconsin Works (W-2), or a program under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA), at least 80 hours each month.
3. Work and take part in an allowable work program for a combined total of 80 hours each month.
For more information about FSET, go to dhs.wisconsin.gov/foodshare/fset.htm.
Who is Exempt from the Work Requirement?
Some adults do not have to meet the work requirement to get FoodShare beneﬁts and are considered exempt.
You may not have to meet the work requirement if any of the following are true:
You are living with a child under age 18 who is part of the same FoodShare household.
You are the primary caretaker for a person who cannot care for himself or herself.
You are the primary caretaker for a child under age 6 who does not live in the home.
You are physically or mentally unable to work. This includes being homeless long- term. Being homeless long- term means you will not have a regular place to stay for the next 30 nights.
You are pregnant.
You are receiving or have applied for unemployment insurance.
You are taking part in an alcohol or other drug abuse (AODA) treatment or rehabilitation program.
You are enrolled in an institution of higher learning at least half-time.
You are age 18 or older attending high school at least half-time.
You are enrolled in W-2 and complying with W-2 requirements.
You are working 30 or more hours per week or are earning wages equal to 30 or more hours per week at the federal minimum wage.

If you meet one of the exemptions listed above, you should contact your agency at the number listed on the top of page 1 of this letter to report the exemption and ﬁnd out what kind of proof is needed.
